title: A nonlinear programming algorithm for solving semidefinite programs via low-rank factorization
contribution: Introduces the low-rank factorization X = RR^T with rank sized by the Barvinok-Pataki bound, solved by an L-BFGS augmented Lagrangian that exploits sparsity, beating spectral bundle and DSDP on large theta, maxcut and bisection SDPs (up to about 500x on G81) without a convergence proof.
problem_entry: Interior-point SDP is too time- and memory-intensive for large combinatorial relaxations; the paper joins the trend toward practically efficient, less theoretically guaranteed methods and frames three questions (size, method, nonconvexity) about the factorized reformulation (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: Replace X >= 0 by a rectangular factor R with r(r+1)/2 <= m columns, so the nonconvex problem is equivalent to the SDP but has nr variables; solve it with a first-order augmented Lagrangian whose evaluations cost O(nonzeros * r) (pp. 3, 5, 8-12).
assumptions: Linearly independent A_i, zero duality gap with attained optima (p. 4); an extreme point exists (Theorem 1, p. 5); regularity for Prop. 4, not guaranteed for theta, so dynamic rank is not used there (p. 14).
proof_devices: Optimality conditions via S = C - sum y_i A_i with grad L = 2SR (Prop. 2, p. 6)
Orthogonal invariance R -> RQ rules out strict local minima (pp. 6-7)
Rank-independent sufficiency: stationary point with S PSD is SDP-optimal (Prop. 3, p. 7)
Zero-column injection into rank r+1 plus second-order conditions forces S PSD (Prop. 4, p. 7)
Flop/space counts for sparse and rank-one data as propositions (Props 5-8, pp. 11-12, 15)
experiments: ANSI C on SGI Origin2000, one processor; Lovasz theta (DIMACS hamming, Gset, 2nd DIMACS), maxcut (torus, Gset up to 20,000 vertices), minimum bisection; SB and DSDP at default parameters, 10-hour limits; accuracy via infeasibility and primal-dual relative difference columns; losses on hamming graphs explained; time-matched truncation of SB (Tables 1-20, pp. 13-26).
positioning: Continues Homer-Peinado and the authors' own Cholesky/NLP SDP work (p. 2); distinguishes from Bentler and the theoretical Lu-Klein (p. 3); concedes dual methods are more valuable when a valid bound is needed (p. 13).
writing: Q1-Q3 questions frame the paper (pp. 2-3); dense explicit hedging (experimental, largely experimental, we feel, pp. 1, 3, 14, 27); strong claims only where measured (p. 27); a warning subsection on gradient-preserved zero columns (pp. 12-13).
limits_future: Slow AL subproblems for theta and bisection, no formal convergence proof, equality-form only; proposes a dual-feasibility safeguard, inequality constraints and a dual low-rank analogue via Pataki's bound on rank(S*) (p. 27).

method_links.note: Known factorization combined with a rank theorem; practical claim carried by experiment with the theory gap printed; baselines at defaults; dynamic rank dropped on theta for weak theory and poor convergence.
Lifted convex object collapsed to a nonconvex factor sized by a theorem; the reformulation serves computation rather than an exact hull.
Accuracy declared on two signals (infeasibility plus primal-dual agreement with another code) and a bound-crossing check.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Valid bound from an inexact first-order solver
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Paper concedes a primal-only method gives no valid bound unless solved exactly; S003 and S013 later supply in-run dual bounds.
Reports SB's objective at the moment LR terminated to separate slow-to-converge from slow-to-get-close.

transferable: Size a factorized variable by a rank theorem (r(r+1)/2 <= m), not by trial (p. 5).
Rank escalation with a zero-column injection test as a certificate of SDP optimality (pp. 7-8).
Initialize away from structured zero patterns by perturbing with a small dense matrix, since gradients preserve zero columns (pp. 12-13, 15).
Add a primal-dual relative difference column and a bound-crossing check when the own method is primal-only (pp. 14, 17).
Report the baseline's value at the time your method stopped (p. 26).

quotes.text: Nonetheless, after much experimentation, we feel that 10−5 is a reasonable amount of infeasibility to require.
Although we have some theoretical justification that explains the observed practical convergence, we do not currently have a formal convergence proof.

title: Local minima and convergence in low-rank semidefinite programming
contribution: Proves that X = RR^T adds no spurious local minima, classifies local minima of rank-constrained SDP (optimal unless on a flat face, for r >= r_{m+1}), proves convergence of a det-perturbed variant of the S001 algorithm, and adds in-run lower bounds with QAP SDPs up to size 40.
problem_entry: Explains the observed but unproved global convergence of the experimental S001 algorithm and fixes its lack of in-run lower bounds (pp. 1, 3).
key_idea: Classify local minima through faces of the SDP feasible set and force rank deficiency of subproblem minimizers by adding a vanishing mu_k det(R^T R) term, which gives asymptotic dual feasibility (pp. 4-11).
assumptions: Primal interior point, attained zero gap (pp. 1-2); r >= r_{m+1} for classification (pp. 6-7), r > r_{m+1} and bounded iterates for Thm 5.3 (p. 11), r > r_{m+2} with a Frobenius ball for Thm 5.4 (p. 12); feasibility/boundedness of S^k not guaranteed, only observed (p. 12).
proof_devices: RR^T = SS^T implies S = RQ, Q orthogonal (Lemma 2.1, p. 4)
No extraneous local minima by a subsequence argument (Prop. 2.3, p. 4)
Pataki rank reduction applied to a sequence, extremality of the limit forces the moves to vanish (Lemma 3.2, pp. 5-6)
Counting unknowns vs equations in system phi(R) gives the r_{m+1} threshold (p. 5)
Zero-column test directions give lim inf S^k . hh^T >= 0; boundedness of S^k by recession-direction contradiction (Thm 4.1, pp. 8-9)
det(I + delta Delta) has no local minimum at 0, used with a Cholesky reparametrization preserving inner products (Lemmas 5.1-5.2, pp. 10-11)
experiments: Same code as S001 on a Pentium 2.4 GHz; certificates primal infeasibility, ||SR||, lambda_min(S); lower bounds by lambda_min shift when trace is constant; 5 maxcut + 5 stable set (Tables 1-2) and QAPR1/QAPR2 for 17 QAPLIB instances, 30 <= l <= 40, up to 6.4 days; nug30 compared with Rendl-Sotirov on a named different machine; QAPR3 excluded with reasons (pp. 13-17).
positioning: Places first-order NLP methods among three SDP method families (p. 2); takes S001 as its own ancestor and corrects its rank choice from r_m to r_{m+1} in print (p. 7); compares QAP bounds with Lin-Saigal, Zhao et al., Rendl-Sotirov (p. 16).
writing: Theorems followed by roughly-speaking readings (p. 7) and named drawbacks (pp. 9, 12); states plainly that experiments use the unperturbed algorithm (p. 13); one proof left to the reader (p. 10).
limits_future: Flat faces can harbour non-global minima (p. 7); det term not implementable stably (p. 13); unproved feasibility/boundedness (p. 12); weaker stable-set duals (p. 15); inequalities open (p. 16); long QAP times (p. 17).

method_links.note: Theory follows the prototype: the convergence proof for S001 comes two years later and covers a slight variant that is not run.
Claim narrowed in print: S001's r >= r_m shown insufficient for the local-minimum guarantee and the implementation changed; unproved conditions labelled as observed.
Hardness of the nonconvex reformulation located in flat faces of the SDP feasible set; aim is algorithm convergence, not an exact reformulation.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Lower bounds during the run by shifting the approximate dual slack by lambda_min when the identity is in the span of the A_i; scaling extends it to 0-1 QPs.

transferable: Vanishing determinant perturbation to force rank deficiency in factorized subproblems (pp. 10-11).
Zero-column test directions to extract dual feasibility from second-order conditions (p. 8).
Replace assumed bounded iterates by a Frobenius-ball constraint at the price of one rank level (p. 12).
In-run certificate triple: primal infeasibility, ||SR||, lambda_min(S) (p. 13).
Turn an approximate dual slack into a valid bound by a lambda_min shift when the trace is constant (p. 14).

quotes.text: In particular, we show that the change of variables does not introduce any extraneous local minima.
While it seems that the extra term is necessary for theoretical convergence, it does not appear to be necessary for practical convergence.

title: Ensemble Pruning Via Semi-definite Programming
contribution: Formulates ensemble pruning as a cardinality-constrained 0-1 QP over a normalized co-error matrix, maps it to max-cut-with-size-k, and solves the SDP relaxation with SDPLR plus randomized rounding, beating greedy pruning heuristics on 24 UCI sets and a 19-category marketing case study.
problem_entry: Large ensembles cost memory and time and can overfit; existing pruning heuristics rely on greedy search without quality guarantees (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Write pruning as min x^T G x with sum x = k, transform to +-1 variables, homogenize with v0 into bordered matrices, relax to an SDP and round as for MC-k (pp. 4-8).
assumptions: Ensemble error approximated by a linear combination of strength and pairwise co-error terms; the diversity term is ad hoc; cardinality constraint needed to avoid the empty solution; equivalence with MC-k holds for optimal sets, not values (pp. 4-7).
proof_devices: n/a for theorems; derivation devices: x = (v+1)/2 substitution and homogenization with v0 into H and D (pp. 6-7)
Relaxing v0 in {-1,1} by sign symmetry, then V = vv^T and dropping rank one (p. 8)
Argument why the MC-k approximation guarantee does not transfer (optimal sets vs values; minimization form) (p. 7)
experiments: 24 UCI data sets, AdaBoost with 100 C4.5 trees pruned to 25, five 10-fold CVs, W-L-T by mean and 95% t test vs diversity and Kappa pruning; timing up to 3,000 classifiers (about a day); DMEF catalog case study with 19 skewed categories, AUC, class-balanced G, Herfindahl index (pp. 9-21).
positioning: Against greedy pruning (Margineantu-Dietterich, Prodromidis et al.) and evolutionary methods; distinct from weight-based ensemble optimization that lacks size control; SDP in ML beside sparse PCA and kernel learning (pp. 2-3).
writing: Applied-ML motivation by examples (p. 2); hedged formulation and scaling claims (pp. 5, 11); table cross-references in the text mismatch the captions (pp. 9-11, 17).
limits_future: No approximation guarantee (p. 7); ad hoc normalization and weights to tune; seek an objective without the cardinality constraint (p. 21); about a day for 3,000 classifiers (p. 11).

method_links.note: A lifted SDP object packages the combinatorial difficulty, but as a heuristic relaxation for rounding, with the guarantee explicitly lost.
Own public solver (SDPLR) used off the shelf in a new domain, with a timing study and no theory.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: An ML subset-selection problem is reformulated as a 0-1 QP and solved with the author's own SDPLR code; only paper in the batch showing this.

transferable: Homogenize a 0/1 quadratic with a cardinality constraint into a +-1 problem with bordered matrices, then relax to an SDP (pp. 6-8).
State whether a borrowed reformulation preserves optimal sets or optimal values before claiming a transferred guarantee (p. 7).
Choose baselines that can be forced to the same output size for a fair comparison (p. 9).
Combine class-specific selection matrices convexly when classes are highly skewed (p. 15).
coauthors: Yi Zhang, W. Nick Street (K. P. Bennett and E. Parrado-Hernandez are the issue editors, p. 1, not authors)

quotes.text: Therefore, if we are able to transform the ensemble pruning formulation so that it fits into the framework of MC-k, we may obtain a good solution for the ensemble pruning problem.
In fact, it seems extremely difficult to derive directly any approximation guarantees for our problem.

title: Solving lift-and-project relaxations of binary integer programs
contribution: Decomposes the Lovasz-Schrijver N(K) and N+(K) relaxations with copy variables and solves them by an augmented Lagrangian with block coordinate descent and PSD projection, proves constant-penalty convergence for linear conic AL, and obtains the then-strongest QAPLIB bounds.
problem_entry: Lift-and-project relaxations are strong in theory but almost never computed because of their size (over 1.7 million constraints); only Dash had studied them computationally (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Introduce Z = YQ (and U = Y for the PSD case) so constraints separate over columns, dualize only the linking equations, and use an augmented Lagrangian instead of subgradient (pp. 4-5, 11-13).
assumptions: Generic 0-1 IP with Ax <= b; K replaced by K-hat = K intersect [0,1] (p. 4); Theorem 3.1 needs full row rank A and Slater points for primal and dual (p. 7); QAP structure removes Z (p. 16).
proof_devices: Theorem 3.1: constant-penalty AL convergence for linear conic programs, extending Poljak-Tret'jakov from the nonnegative orthant to general cones (pp. 7, 9-11)
Monotonicity inequality for dual iterates (Lemma 3.2, p. 10) and exactness at a dual optimum (Lemma 3.3, p. 10)
Telescoping ||lambda^{k+1}-lambda*||^2 <= ||lambda^k-lambda*||^2 - sigma^2||b-Ay^k||^2 gives Ay^k -> b (Prop. 3.4, pp. 10-11)
Each iterate is exactly primal-dual optimal for the problem with right-hand side Ay^k (Lemma 3.5, p. 11)
AL step shown equal to a bundle step without the bundle approximation (eq. (25), pp. 8-9)
Projection of a nonsymmetric matrix onto the PSD cone equals projection of its symmetric part (p. 13)
experiments: ANSI C, Pentium 4 2.4 GHz, CPLEX 8.1 pivoting QP with warm starts, LAPACK (pp. 13-14); 26 DIMACS stable-set graphs, Erdos-Turan n = 60-150, generated markshare-type 0-1 instances, 91 QAPLIB instances; baselines CPLEX dual simplex (default and steepest edge, 15,000 s), tuned volume subgradient with surpass times, CSDP (memory failure), GLB/KCCEB/RSB and later Hahn level-2 RLT; losses printed (pp. 14-23).
positioning: In the lift-and-project lineage (Balas, Sherali-Adams, Lovasz-Schrijver, Lasserre, Bienstock-Zuckerberg); AL for LP not new but computationally unexplored, AL for SDP presented for the first time (pp. 1-2); KCCEB equal in theory but QAP-specific, AL general (pp. 16, 23); N+ beats RSB (p. 23).
writing: Anticipates the objection that an NLP method for linear conic problems may seem counterintuitive (p. 6); every implementation choice paired with theory and its practical override (pp. 14-15); claims kept at approximately solved (p. 19); late results added with provenance (p. 23).
limits_future: N+ not optimized fully (p. 19); AL slower than subgradient on Erdos-Turan (pp. 17-18); no gain on markshare (p. 20); eigendecompositions dominate for QAP (pp. 23-24); future: special QP solvers, mixed binary-continuous and nonconvex QP relaxations, block-angular conic problems (p. 24).

method_links.note: One lifted object Y = [1 x^T; x xx^T] carries the strength; work goes into attacking it with a tractable method; conclusion aims the machinery at mixed binary-continuous and nonconvex QP.
Slow initial subgradient experiments motivated the AL choice; practice overrides theory with the override printed (sigma growth, one BCD cycle); best public codes as baselines.
Computed N+ above theta, which theory forbids at optimality, is read as incomplete optimization; theory-practice gaps with KCCEB attributed to numerics.
Uses a generator for small hard 0-1 programs (markshare type), but the pool is mainly public libraries and not filtered to baseline failures.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: AL chosen partly because it yields primal and dual solutions as well as dual bounds; complements S001 p. 13 and S003 p. 14.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Variable splitting by copies to decompose a lifted relaxation
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Z = YQ makes the LS LP separable over columns; U = Y moves the PSD constraint into its own projection block.

transferable: Copy-variable decomposition (Z = YQ, U = Y) and dualize only the copy equations (pp. 4-5, 12).
One block-coordinate cycle per AL subproblem with a warm-startable pivoting QP solver (pp. 13-14).
Project a nonsymmetric matrix onto the PSD cone via its symmetric part (p. 13).
Constant-penalty AL convergence by a telescoping residual argument (pp. 10-11).
Surpass-time columns in head-to-head bound tables, with the baseline tuned and the tuning disclosed (pp. 17-18).

quotes.text: The key idea is a restructuring of the relaxations, which isolates the complicating constraints and allows for a Lagrangian approach.
This demonstrates that lift-and-project operators are not always able to strengthen the LP relaxation of an IP.
